title: The Secret Playlist
premise: Hazel Marchetti has perfected invisibility, but when a mysterious group chat called 'The Secret Playlist' starts sending song-linked predictions that come true, Hazel and four other overlooked students are pulled into a game neither of them understands. The chat's final prophecy demands they win the school's Battle of the Bands — a contest that secretly decides which of them survives a bargain made years before their birth by their parents. As Hazel bakes truth-telling loaves to bind the group into a real family, they discover the playlist's curator is a dying classmate trading borrowed time for one perfect memory. In the end, Hazel sacrifices their own spot in the future — not their life, but everyone's memories of them — to break the bargain, winning both championships and learning that being forgotten is the price of having finally mattered.
about_author: Astrid Kavanagh is a former radio DJ turned novelist who grew up above her family's bakery in coastal Oregon, where she learned that every recipe hides a confession. She writes stories about quiet kids, loud music, and the families we assemble from strangers.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Opening at 4 a.m. in the bakery, Hazel kneads grief-bread for a classmate's canceled recital, establishing their rule: bake feelings, share nothing. At school they stay invisible while the popular world churns. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety, and the first hint that Hazel's bread does something impossible — it makes people feel what Hazel feels.

chapters.title: Unknown Number, Five Members
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A group chat invites Hazel by name alongside four strangers: Theo the dropout drummer, Priya the debate champion, Marcus the janitor's son, and Wren, who hasn't spoken in two years. The first message predicts tomorrow's fire drill to the minute. It happens exactly. Emotional beat: unease curdling into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Track One: Something Borrowed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The chat sends each member a song; Theo's predicts his father's layoff hours before it happens. He tries to warn him and fails, realizing predictions can't be outrun, only prepared for. He seeks out the other chat members for the first time. Emotional beat: helplessness transformed into the first fragile alliance.

chapters.title: The Rye That Tells the Truth
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel bakes a loaf laced with longing after overhearing Priya cry in the stairwell; whoever eats it confesses. Priya admits she's been faking her perfect life since her sister left. Hazel breaks their own silence rule to sit with her. Emotional beat: the cost of connection begins to outweigh the comfort of hiding.

chapters.title: Battle of the Bands (The One That Doesn't Matter)
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The school announces its annual Battle of the Bands, a joke contest nobody respectable enters. The chat messages: ENTER. Marcus, who fixes instruments but never plays them, argues they have no band, no songs, no chance. Wren silently posts a video of herself singing, her first communication in years. Emotional beat: terror and thrill braided together.

chapters.title: Wren, Unmuted
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback to why Wren stopped speaking — a viral humiliation engineered by her former best friend, now student body president Delia Voss. The chat's songs keep predicting small mercies for Wren, and she begins to believe the universe owes her something. She agrees to join the band on one condition: they take down Delia. Emotional beat: rage as a survival strategy starting to thaw.

chapters.title: Rehearsal in the Boiler Room
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Five misfits cram into the boiler room with borrowed instruments and zero chemistry. Hazel brings bread that tastes like courage; it works too well, and Theo nearly gets caught breaking back into school. They name themselves The Secret Playlist without admitting why. Emotional beat: found family forming out of shared embarrassment and laughter.

chapters.title: Track Seven: The One About Us
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A prediction arrives about the five of them — a song titled with all their names — dated three months out, labeled FINAL TRACK. Priya cross-references past predictions and finds a pattern: every song predicted someone's death or disappearance, always softened, always survived. Except this one has no softening. Emotional beat: dread arriving in an ordinary moment.

chapters.title: Delia's Counterplay
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Delia Voss discovers the boiler room rehearsals and weaponizes the administration: permits revoked, instruments confiscated, Wren threatened with expulsion over the old incident. Marcus uses his janitor keys and knowledge of the building's bones to keep them one step ahead. Emotional beat: the enemy is not the prophecy but the people who benefit from the status quo.

chapters.title: What Our Parents Signed
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Investigating the chat's origin, Hazel finds a photograph in the bakery's attic: their parents, young, with the same five surnames on a contract — a bargain trading their children's futures for their own survival during a disaster only half-remembered. The chat was created by someone collecting on the debt. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as a trap.

chapters.title: Interlude: Bread for the Dying
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel traces the chat's IP to a hospital room and finds Eli Sandoval — a classmate who's been 'sick' all year, actually kept alive by the same bargain, spending his borrowed months curating predictions. He doesn't want to hurt anyone; he wants the band to win so the contract names a new bearer and he can finally rest. Emotional beat: compassion for the antagonist, horror at the math.

chapters.title: The Championship That Does Matter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Eli explains the second championship hidden inside the first: if the band wins Battle of the Bands, the contract transfers; if they lose, the debt collects randomly among the five. Theo, whose brother died before him because of a similar family bargain, refuses to let fate choose. Emotional beat: defiance crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Songs We Stole From Each Other
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Songwriting montage: each member contributes a track built from another member's worst memory, transmuted. Wren writes Hazel's isolation into melody; Hazel bakes Wren's voice back into confidence. The setlist becomes a map of their wounds. Emotional beat: art as mutual rescue, intimacy deepening between Hazel and Wren.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Last Loaf
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. After a near-disaster gig at the boardwalk, Hazel and Wren kiss in the flour-dusted dark of the closed bakery. But Hazel realizes the FINAL TRACK prediction is counting down faster than the calendar says it should — Eli is running out of time and accelerating the schedule. Emotional beat: joy shadowed by a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Delia, tipped off by a jealous ex-bandmate, destroys their gear and leaks the contract photo, turning parents against children — Hazel's own mother admits she signed, believing she was saving Hazel's life. The band fractures; Wren accuses Hazel of knowing all along. Emotional beat: betrayal cutting deepest where trust grew thickest.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Bake
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Alone, Hazel bakes through the night — bread for each member carrying what they need to hear — and delivers it door to door like contraband apologies. One by one they return to the boiler room. Eli, visibly fading, gives them the last prediction: the venue, the hour, the song that must be played. Emotional beat: forgiveness as an act of stubborn love.

chapters.title: Qualifiers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With repaired junk instruments, the band claws through qualifiers against Delia's hand-picked headliners. Mid-song, Wren speaks publicly for the first time in two years, dismantling Delia's old lie in front of the whole school. They advance — barely. Emotional beat: reclamation, voice recovered, old wound cauterized in public.

chapters.title: FINAL TRACK
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Finals night. The chat goes silent mid-set — Eli is dying now, the contract unraveling early. The band plays the unnamed final song, and the championship magic activates: the audience forgets them note by note as the contract demands a bearer. Hazel understands the fine print at last and steps forward alone. Emotional beat: sacrificial clarity, love choosing its price.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel takes the contract, redirecting the debt onto themself: not death, but erasure — every memory of Hazel will dissolve when the last song ends. They finish the set as the crowd's eyes slide away, baking one final loaf no one will remember eating. Wren fights toward the stage, forgetting why she's crying. Emotional beat: heartbreak rendered tender, victory indistinguishable from loss.

chapters.title: Encore for Nobody
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The band wins both championships — the trophy and the lives — but cannot remember who the fifth member was. Only the bread remains, still warm, still tasting of someone. Wren finds Hazel's recipe journal, where the last page reads: 'If you're reading this, sing it back.' Emotional beat: grief with a keyhole of hope.

chapters.title: Baked Into the Crumb
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The four follow the journal's instructions — a recipe requiring all their hands, sung aloud — and the act of making it together stitches Hazel back into existence, because the contract bound a family, not individuals, and families don't forget on command. Hazel returns mid-laugh, remembered imperfectly but entirely. Emotional beat: resurrection through collective memory.

chapters.title: Track Zero
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Epilogue at dawn in the bakery. Eli's memorial bench holds the championship trophy; the group chat sends one last message — a blank track, meaning the future is unwritten. Hazel, no longer invisible, chooses to be seen: sign on the door, name on the bread, Wren's hand in theirs. Emotional beat: peace earned, the playlist finally theirs to compose.
